target_customer: Cattle owners and dairies who feed a supplement, with revenue partly from carbon or methane credit programs
problem: Enteric fermentation in cattle produces large methane emissions. Alga makes a kelp or algae based feed additive, about 0.5 percent of diet, that it says cuts methane by up to 97 percent.
business_model: Feed additive sales to cattle producers, paired with methane credit programs via partners

founders.name: Alexander Brown
prior_employers: Chief of Staff at an unnamed software company
education: Undergraduate in life sciences and economics (institution not listed)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; named co-founder and CEO in TechCrunch April 2023.

founders.name: Daria Balatsky
founders.background_notes: YC page says physical chemist who synthesized drugs for kidney disease and studied quantum materials.

founders.name: Caroline McKeon
founders.background_notes: YC page lists physical chemistry training including quantum mechanical electronic structure theory.

competitors.name: CH4 Global
competitors.what: Asparagopsis seaweed based methane reducing feed additive
competitors.funding_then: $13M Series A announced October 2021 led by DCVC

competitors.name: Rumin8
competitors.what: Synthetic replica of the Asparagopsis bioactive for ruminant methane
competitors.funding_then: Equity funding from Prelude Ventures and a Sentient WA fund, reported July 18, 2022 (a few months after the batch)

technical_complexity.rationale: Requires biology, live animal trials, scalable algae or kelp production and proof of methane reduction that holds in commercial feeding, which is hard for a six person team.

defensibility.rationale: Trial data, production know how and any approvals are hard to copy, but many additive approaches (3-NOP, Asparagopsis, plant extracts) compete and none was a clear winner.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Well funded rivals raised larger rounds (CH4 Global $29M Series B in August 2023). No acquisition of Alga was found; it partnered with 3Degrees to launch a program.

market_need_then: Livestock methane is a large share of agricultural emissions, and the seed announcement cites USDA Climate Smart Commodities support. Collaborative Fund's post notes red seaweed is slow and capital intensive to grow, framing demand for faster scaling options.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain climate and agriculture language; tagline we stop cows from burping methane

branding.brand_signature: The line we stop cows from burping methane
branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage on the idea itself (TechCrunch headline featuring Honey the Cow, The Hustle, Earth.com) and an Unreasonable Group affiliation.

brand_strength.rationale: The cow burp pitch is memorable and drew mainstream coverage, though the name itself is generic.

outcome_analysis: Alga raised a seed round led by Collaborative Fund in April 2023, totaling $4M raised per TechCrunch, after academic trials that reported undetectable methane from beef cattle. It was preparing commercial pilots, partnered with 3Degrees to bring the product to market, and is hiring in 2026. Company claims on methane reduction are not independently verified, and rivals with larger rounds compete for the same buyers, so scale of adoption is still unproven.
notes: TechCrunch and Collaborative Fund (both April 6, 2023) state $4M raised in total; Collaborative Fund calls it a $4M seed while TechCrunch says $4M is the company total, so the seed amount is left null. Aggregators (CB Insights $4.85M over 6 rounds, Employbl $4.5M with a $500K pre-seed, a later September 2025 Unreasonable Food entry) are unverified. Rumin8 source is dated a few months after the batch. A 2021 founding year comes from aggregators.
